discovered-from:LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want each provider entry in a model's `providers`
list to declare the priorities it may serve (`priorities: [low, medium]`), and
to **delete `priority_routes` entirely**, so that priority routing is declared
once, in one place, in the provider definition I am already editing — instead
of maintaining a second, name-referencing index that duplicates the chain and
is easy to drift or get wrong.

## Problem statement

Priority routing is currently declared twice for every model in
`proxy/config.yaml`:

1. `models.<name>.providers` — the ordered provider definitions; and
2. `models.<name>.priority_routes` — a map from priority to an ordered list of
   provider **names**, resolved back against (1) at request time by
   `proxy/proxy/priority.py::_resolve_chain_entries`.

This gives two competing sources of truth for the same chain, and the operator
has to keep them synchronised by hand. Concrete mess re-verified against the
tree on 2026-10-24:

- `plan`, `author` and `code` carry **byte-identical** 7-entry `providers`
  lists (`plan == author == code` compares `True`), each with the **identical**
  5-name `low` list — 21 provider definitions and 15 repeated names. Verified
  provider order: `local-qwen3`, `munitoai-free`, `opencode-go-3`,
  `opencode-go-2`, `opencode-go`, `munitoai`, `deepseek-flash`.
- Membership in a priority chain is invisible from the provider definition: to
  answer "is `munitoai` used for low work?" you must read a different block.
- Name references add a failure mode with no upside: an unresolvable name is
  logged as `priority_routes: unknown provider name %r … skipping entry` and
  routing silently continues with a shorter chain.
- A new provider inherits priority membership only if someone remembers to add
  its name to the right list(s) — and forgetting means it is silently absent
  from (or, for a paid tier, silently present in) a `low` chain.
- Ordering is likewise stated twice: `providers` order *and* each
  `priority_routes` list order, which must agree.
- Nothing validates `priority_routes` at load: `_validate_config`
  (`proxy/proxy/utils.py:650`) validates prompts, chain-hold and compaction,
  but nothing provider- or priority-shaped.

## Operator decisions (recorded)

- **Delete `priority_routes`.** No compatibility shim, no override path, no
  "both work" period: the two-representations problem is the whole complaint.
- **Priority membership lives only on provider definitions**, as a
  `priorities` key whose value is a **list** of valid priorities
  (`[low, medium, high]`, `[medium, high]`, …).
- **No implication between tiers.** A provider labelled `medium` is *not*
  thereby eligible for `low`; membership is exactly the list written. (An
  earlier idea — a scalar threshold where `medium` implied `low` — was rejected
  because it would have put the paid `munitoai` / `deepseek-flash` tiers into
  the `low` chain, breaking AC6 of LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX.)
- **Per-model divergence is a requirement, not an accident.** The label sits on
  each model's own inline provider entry, so *plan* may later add an expensive
  model while *code* keeps the current set and *author* gains a
  less code-oriented one, without touching the other models.

## Design

Resolution becomes a filter over the model's own provider list, in list order
(no name lookup, no rank table, no monotonicity assumption):

```python
chain(P) = [p for p in providers if P in p["priorities"]]   # order = providers order
```

- Model-level opt-in, fail-closed: if **any** provider in a model declares
  `priorities`, **every** provider in that model must declare it (otherwise the
  chain would depend on an implicit default, which is exactly the silent-leak
  bug class this item removes). A model that declares no `priorities` anywhere
  keeps today's behaviour: every provider eligible for every priority (this is
  what `embed`, `github` and `private` do today — they have no
  `priority_routes`). That legacy full-list default is therefore scoped to
  *unlabelled* models only.
- **No implicit fallback for a labelled model.** Today
  `priority.py::effective_chain_for_request` re-adds the full `providers` list
  when the chain it obtained is empty (`if not chain: chain = providers`). For a
  labelled model an empty filtered chain must **not** be widened that way —
  that is the same silent leak in another disguise. See Q6 for the open
  question on what a labelled model with no provider for a priority should do
  (load-time rejection vs. request-time exhaustion).
- A model that still contains `priority_routes` must fail at load with a
  migration message (fail-closed; a stale overlay must not silently lose its
  routing).
- Validation (load-time `ValueError`): non-list value, empty list, unknown
  priority name, duplicate entry, and the partially-labelled-model rule above.

Behaviour-equivalent target for the shipped config (this is the refactor, not a
routing change):

| Model | `low` | `medium` / `high` |
|---|---|---|
| `plan`, `author`, `code` | `local-qwen3`, `munitoai-free`, `opencode-go-3`, `opencode-go-2`, `opencode-go` | full 7-entry `providers` list |
| `compact` | `opencode-go-compact`, `deepseek-flash-compact` | full 2-entry `providers` list |
| `embed`, `github`, `private` | full `providers` list | full `providers` list |

⇒ labels: `local-qwen3`, `munitoai-free`, `opencode-go-3`, `opencode-go-2`,
`opencode-go`, `opencode-go-compact`, `deepseek-flash-compact` =
`[low, medium, high]`; `munitoai`, `deepseek-flash` = `[medium, high]`.
`local-embed`, `github-primary`, `local-qwen3` (private) need no labels.

## Scope

In scope:

- `proxy/config.yaml`: add `priorities` to every provider entry of the
  priority-routed models; delete the four `priority_routes` blocks and their
  now-stale rationale comments —
  `plan` line 569, `author` line 731, `code` line 900, `compact` line 950
  (whose comment "Declared explicitly to satisfy the per-model
  `priority_routes` schema (AC2)" at 946-949 also goes); move/retain the
  rationale in the provider definitions and the docs.
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py`: delete `_resolve_chain_entries` (342); replace
  `provider_chain_for_priority` (379) with the filter; drop the empty-chain
  full-list fallback for labelled models in `effective_chain_for_request`
  (447, fallback at 460-462); update the module docstring (32-41),
  `priority_routing_profile` (274) and `apply_local_preference`-adjacent
  docstrings that currently document `priority_routes` as the mechanism.
- `proxy/proxy/utils.py`: add the provider `priorities` /
  removed-`priority_routes` validation and wire it into `_validate_config`
  (650), following the existing delegate pattern (`_validate_chain_hold_config`
  660, `_validate_compaction_config` 674, `_validate_prompt_configs` 689) —
  i.e. a `validate_priority_config(cfg) -> list[str]` in `provider.py`
  validated from `utils.py`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`: **comment-only** edits — the two call-site
  comments name `priority_routes` (`8186-8188`, `8827-8829`). The functional
  integration is `effective_chain_for_request` (imported at line 48, called at
  8196 and 8837) and needs no change beyond the above.
- Docs: `proxy/README.md` (line 18 bullet; 1188-1193 "Each model may declare
  `priority_routes` (AC2)" paragraph), `proxy/docs/routing.md` (the off-peak
  section at 225-260, which writes the `low` chain as `low: [...]` and must
  describe the labels instead), provider field table in `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`
  (97-108 — the `| Field | Type | Required | Description |` table where
  `priorities` belongs, next to `max_context_tokens`). `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md`
  does **not** exist yet (LP-0MVDW6Z870066DEY is at `plan_complete`), so it is
  cross-referenced rather than edited.
- Tests:
  - `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py`: rewrite `TestProviderChains`
    (164-200, currently asserts name resolution / unknown-name skip) and
    `TestModeRemoval::test_models_declare_priority_routes` (382-389, asserts the
    live config has `priority_routes.low`) — AC1 forbids the string anywhere.
  - `proxy/tests/test_low_priority_offpeak_fallback.py`: the `_target_chain_entries`
    shim (131-141, synthesises `priority_routes`) and
    `TestLiveConfigInvariants::test_fully_paid_tiers_never_enter_a_low_chain`
    (194-204, reads `routes = model.get("priority_routes")`); the remaining
    `TestTargetChainShape` (153), `TestWindowGating` (228), `TestFailoverScope`
    (281) and `TestRoutingProfileDocs` (331) assertions keep their intent while
    the chains are derived from labels.
  - `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py`: whole-entry equality against
    literals — `providers[1] == MUNITOAI_FREE_ENTRY` (89, 129) and
    `providers[paid_index] == MUNITOAI_ENTRY` (110, 133). The fixtures must gain
    the new `priorities` key (or the assertions become key-subset checks) or
    they break on the re-labelled config.

Out of scope:

- Any routing behaviour change: no chain membership, order, window, budget or
  failover semantics change. `available_times` line count must be unchanged
  (136 matching lines across `proxy/tests/*.py` today; the config lines
  themselves are byte-frozen by AC4).
- Per-priority *ordering* (e.g. `munitoai` first for `high` only). It was
  expressible only via `priority_routes`, and is deliberately dropped; it is
  not used by any model today. Record it as a known limitation, not a gap.
- DRYing the duplicated per-model provider definitions into YAML anchors or a
  shared provider library (see the anchor caveat in Q5).

## Constraints

- **Behaviour-neutral by construction.** No chain membership, order, window,
  budget or failover change; AC3 (frozen equivalence) and AC8 (unchanged
  off-peak intent) are the gate, and AC4 forbids any non-`priorities` config
  diff.
- **One mechanism, no compatibility window.** `priority_routes` is deleted
  outright (no shim, no override, no deprecation phase); a stale config that
  still declares it must fail loudly at load with a migration message.
- **No tier implication.** A label lists exactly the priorities a provider may
  serve; `medium` never implies `low`.
- **Per-model labels are independent.** No shared/global membership table, and
  no change may introduce cross-model coupling.
- **Repository boundaries.** Implementation touches only `proxy/`; agent
  infrastructure (`.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/`) is out of bounds and issues
  there are reported, not edited.
- **Tests run through the test skill** (`/skill:test`), never ad-hoc `pytest`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `priority_routes` appears nowhere in the repository: not in `proxy/config.yaml`,
   not in any Python source, test, or documentation (`git grep -n priority_routes`
   over the tracked tree returns nothing outside `.worklog/`). Re-verified
   baseline today (`git grep -c`, 27 matching lines in 6 files): `config.yaml`
   5 (569/731/900/949/950), `priority.py` 7, `provider.py` 2 (8187/8828),
   `README.md` 3, `test_priority_routing.py` 8,
   `test_low_priority_offpeak_fallback.py` 2.
2. Every provider entry of `plan`, `author`, `code` and `compact` declares a
   `priorities` list; `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` declare exactly
   `[medium, high]` and appear in no `low` chain; all other entries declare
   `[low, medium, high]`.
3. An equivalence test derives every chain from the `priorities` labels and
   asserts byte-identical equality with the pre-change chains, frozen as
   literals in the test: `low` = the 5-entry list for plan/author/code and the
   2-entry list for `compact`; `medium`/`high` = the full `providers` list for
   every model; `embed`, `github`, `private` = full list for all three
   priorities.
4. `git diff` for `proxy/config.yaml` shows **zero** changed `available_times`
   lines, and every provider entry's non-`priorities` keys are byte-identical
   to before.
5. Load-time validation rejects, each with a test: a non-list `priorities`
   value; an empty list; an unknown priority name; a duplicate entry; a model
   where some but not all providers declare `priorities`; and a model that
   still declares `priority_routes` (clear migration message naming the
   replacement key).
6. `provider_chain_for_priority` contains no name lookup and no provider-name
   warning path (`_resolve_chain_entries` is deleted); chain order is the
   model's `providers` order, proved by a test using an out-of-alphabetical
   order.
7. Per-model divergence is proved by a test: two models with identical provider
   lists except for one provider's `priorities` value resolve to different
   chains, with no cross-model coupling.
8. Priors preserved: `proxy/tests/test_low_priority_offpeak_fallback.py` passes
   unchanged in intent — in-window eligibility, out-of-window skip-and-fall-
   through, per-key-429 sibling failover, same-domain-5xx exclusion — now
   expressed through `priorities` labels.
9. Docs: `README.md`, `docs/routing.md`, `MODEL_ADD.md` and the `priority.py`
   docstrings describe `priorities` as the one mechanism, state that
   `priority_routes` is removed and how to migrate, and record that
   per-priority ordering is not supported.
10. Full suite green via `/skill:test`; the change is behaviour-neutral
    (no routing, window, budget or failover change is claimed or observed).
11. A labelled model never silently widens a filtered chain: an empty
    `chain(P)` is either a load-time error or an explicit request-time
    exhaustion, never a fallback to the full `providers` list — with a test for
    the chosen rule (see Q6, pending producer confirmation).

## Key Files (predicted; line numbers verified 2026-10-24)

- `proxy/config.yaml` — `embed` 338, `github` 346, `private` 357 (unlabelled,
  unchanged); `plan` 383 (providers 388-568, `priority_routes` 569, stale
  rationale comment 550-568); `author` 584 (`priority_routes` 731); `code` 753
  (`priority_routes` 900); `compact` 922 (providers 923-948, `priority_routes`
  950 with its 946-949 AC2 comment).
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — module docstring 32-41,
  `priority_routing_profile` 274, `_resolve_chain_entries` 342 (delete),
  `provider_chain_for_priority` 379, `effective_chain_for_request` 447 with the
  empty-chain fallback at 460-462.
- `proxy/proxy/utils.py` — `_validate_config` 650 and its delegate pattern
  (660 / 674 / 689).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — comment-only 8186-8188, 8827-8829; import 48 and
  calls 8196 / 8837 unchanged.
- `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py` — `TestProviderChains` 164-200,
  `TestModeRemoval::test_models_declare_priority_routes` 382-389.
- `proxy/tests/test_low_priority_offpeak_fallback.py` — `_target_chain_entries`
  131-141, `TestTargetChainShape` 153, `TestLiveConfigInvariants` 170
  (priority_routes read at 199), `TestWindowGating` 228, `TestFailoverScope`
  281, `TestRoutingProfileDocs` 331.
- `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py` — entry literals 29-70 and the
  equality assertions at 89, 110, 129, 133.
- `proxy/README.md` 18 and 1188-1193; `proxy/docs/routing.md` 225-260;
  `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` 97-108.

## Effort and risk

- **Effort: S** — net code deletion (a ~30-line name resolver replaced by a
  filter), config re-labelling, validation (~20 lines), docs, tests.
- **Risk: Low** — behaviour-neutral by construction and proved by the frozen
  equivalence test (AC3) plus the unchanged off-peak tests (AC8). The two real
  hazards are (a) a silent default for an unlabelled provider in a labelled
  model, removed by AC5's fail-closed validation, and (b) the empty-filtered-
  chain widening at `effective_chain_for_request` 460-462, removed by AC11.
  Secondary hazard: whole-entry test literals
  (`test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py`) fail the moment the config gains
  `priorities` — a mechanical fix, but a build-red window if forgotten.
- **Scope-creep risk: moderate.** The refactor makes the duplicated per-model
  provider blocks painful to read (21 near-identical definitions), which will
  tempt a YAML-anchor/shared-library dedup in the same change. Do not: Q5 shows
  an anchor shares `priorities` and would silently destroy per-model routing.
  Record any such idea as a new linked work item instead.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX** — Enable low-priority fallback to opencode-go during
  its off-peak windows (**completed**; source of this item). Its AC6 (paid tiers
  never in a `low` chain) and AC8 (live-window verification via child
  LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO, also **completed**) constrain this refactor: the derived
  chains must be identical to the ones that item shipped.
- **LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA** — Priority-based routing replacing fast/cheap mode
  (completed): introduced `priority_routes` (its AC2 allowed "an equivalent
  per-provider eligibility field"); this item adopts that alternative and
  removes the list form.
- **LP-0MVDW6Z870066DEY** — Consolidate and document the provider
  fallback-chain configuration model (open, `plan_complete`): the new
  `priorities` field belongs in that reference document; sequence so the two do
  not contradict.
- **LP-0MVF4FIP1001RD8P** — Quota-aware OpenCode Go surge (completed): touched
  the same window-eligibility predicate; confirms `available_times` stays a
  dynamic gate, independent of this static membership label.
- **LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1** — Test: off-peak low-priority fallback gating
  (completed): owns the window-gating assertions that AC8 must keep passing.
- **LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I** — Add opencode-go to low-priority routes (off-peak)
  (completed): the config edit that produced the current 5-entry `low` chains.
- **LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29** — Stale `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` fixtures
  (open, low): same "config schema moved on, fixtures did not" failure pattern;
  not a blocker.

## Sequencing

No hard blocker. LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO (live-window verification) and
LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX (the parent fallback work) are both **completed**, so the
conditional "either order is safe" no longer applies: this item can run now.
If LP-0MVDW6Z870066DEY (provider fallback-chain reference doc) starts first,
land the `priorities` wording there and reference it from here to avoid
contradictory documentation.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1** – Test: off-peak low-priority fallback gating (completed)
- **LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I** – Add opencode-go to low-priority routes (off-peak) (completed)
- **LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA** – Priority-based routing replacing fast/cheap mode (X-Priority header + per-model priority tiers) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- No relevant repository file matches: the automated scan's three hits are the
  unrelated `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts*.txt` prompt
  corpora (matched on generic tokens such as `absent`/`ac2`).

## Duplicate-work check

`wl search "priority_routes" --json` (12 hits) plus a keyword sweep of the
`priorities` / provider-chain vocabulary found **no item satisfying this item's
ACs**: LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA *introduced* `priority_routes` and is closed;
LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX / LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I only edited chain *membership*; and
LP-0MVDW6Z870066DEY documents the fallback-chain model without removing
`priority_routes`. No overlap, no rewrite needed.

## Appendix: design questions & decisions

### Q1. Scalar threshold (`priority: medium` ⇒ also `low`) or explicit list?
**Decision: explicit list.** Rejected the threshold: (a) the operator's stated
implication direction (`medium` implies `low`) would have admitted the paid
`munitoai` / `deepseek-flash` tiers to the `low` chain, breaking
LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX AC6; (b) the workable direction (`low` implies medium/high)
is only a compression of the general case and would re-introduce a hidden
implication between tiers, which the operator explicitly does not want; (c) a
monotone interval cannot express "medium + high but not low" plus a future
"low only" entry in the same model.

### Q2. Key name?
**`priorities`** — a list-valued key; `priority` (singular) reads like
a scalar and was ambiguous about implication direction. Document it in the
`MODEL_ADD.md` provider field table.

### Q3. What about a model that declares no `priorities` at all?
Full `providers` list for every priority — today's behaviour for `embed`,
`github`, `private`. But a *partially* labelled model is a load-time error
(model-level opt-in), so adding a provider never silently joins or leaves a
chain.

### Q4. Keep a `priority_routes` escape hatch for per-priority ordering?
**No.** The operator's reason for this item is that two representations are
confusing. Per-priority ordering is unused today; record it as unsupported and
revisit only if a real need appears.

### Q5. Caveat if someone later DRYs the duplicated provider dicts
A YAML anchor (or a shared provider library) shares the whole dict including
`priorities`, so per-model labels require either un-anchoring or
a per-model `priorities` override merged over the anchor. Recorded so a future
dedup does not silently destroy per-model routing.

### Q6. OPEN QUESTION — what does an *empty* `chain(P)` mean for a labelled model?
Discovered during intake review (2026-10-24): today
`effective_chain_for_request` (`priority.py:460-462`) re-adds the full
`providers` list whenever the selected chain is empty. For an unlabelled model
that is the documented backward-compatible default; for a labelled model whose
providers all omit `P` it is a silent widening to the paid tiers — the same
bug class this item removes. It is not exercised by the shipped config (every
model labels a provider for every priority), so AC3/AC4 are unaffected.

Options:

- **(a) Load-time rejection + no runtime widening (recommended).** Validation
  requires ≥1 provider per priority for a labelled model, and
  `effective_chain_for_request` returns the filtered chain as-is for labelled
  models. Rationale: the cheap window (`server.priority_window`, local
  01:00-10:00) caps *every* request to `low`, so a model with no `low`-eligible
  provider would be unusable for nine hours a day — failing at startup is far
  better than a 503 storm at 02:00.
- **(b) Allow empty chains, no widening.** Return `[]`; the existing exhaustion
  path reports it as a request-time 503. Allows a deliberately restrictive
  model, at the cost of a runtime failure mode that only appears inside the
  cheap window.
- **(c) Keep the full-list fallback for empty chains.** Preserves today's
  code path exactly, but re-introduces the silent paid-tier leak this item
  exists to remove — contradicts Q3's fail-closed rule.

**Recommended:** (a) — fail closed at load, and never widen a labelled model's
chain at request time.
**Status:** awaiting producer confirmation; AC11 is written to accept (a) and
must be tightened if (b) or (c) is chosen.

### Q7. Scope corrections found while verifying the tree
Not operator questions, recorded for traceability: (i) `provider.py` carries two
`priority_routes` *comments* (8186-8188, 8827-8829) which AC1's repo-wide grep
also covers, though the original brief listed provider.py as "no change
expected"; (ii) `test_munitoai_fallback_chain.py` asserts whole-entry equality
against literals and therefore breaks when `priorities` is added; (iii)
`test_priority_routing.py::TestModeRemoval::test_models_declare_priority_routes`
(382-389) was missing from the test scope. All three are now in Scope and Key
Files.
data.title: Replace priority_routes with a per-provider priorities list

data.description:
# Intake brief — Slot-sweep harness cannot exercise local concurrency: add a warm-start / staggered-arrival mode

**Headline:** Make the slot-sweep harness land requests on the local backend under concurrency by adding a warm-start priming gate (proves `cold_start.is_cold() == False` via a completed local prefill) plus a configurable `--stagger-seconds`, so N=2/N=3 runs report `local_stream_share > 0` with ≥2 concurrent local streams and auditable per-request resolved models.

## Problem statement

The controlled N=2/N=3 slot sweep (LP-0MVK096GF0038FTH) produced **local stream share 0.0%** at both counts: every completed benchmark stream was served by a remote provider, so no local TTFT/decode metrics exist and the concurrency-vs-capacity projection (N=2 denies ~19.7% of session-minutes, N=3 ~6.7%) is untestable with the harness as configured. The root cause is structural: each slot-count restart re-arms the proxy's cold-start admission window (`proxy/proxy/cold_start.py`, cap = 1 concurrent local dispatch until the first local prefill completes and calls `mark_warm`), and the harness launches `--concurrency N` inside that window. Because even the first request never completed a local prefill within the run (observed `backend busy (health check timeout)` for the whole window), `mark_warm` never fired and cold cap never lifted — so a fixed 60 s stagger (already present as `INTER_REQUEST_GAP_S`) did not and cannot fix it.

## Users

- **Producer / capacity owner** (rgardler/agents assessing `session_slot_pool_size`): needs a trustworthy N=2-vs-N=3 local-latency comparison to re-decide the slot count (reopening conditions in `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` depend on this item).
  - *User story:* "As a capacity owner, I want the slot sweep to exercise ≥2 concurrent local streams so the N=2-vs-N=3 decision is based on local TTFT/decode data, not remote fallback numbers."
- **Benchmark operator** (agent running the sweep in a quiet window): needs a single deterministic command that lands requests locally without manual heroics.
  - *User story:* "As a benchmark operator, I want one flag such as `--warm-start` plus `--stagger-seconds` so each slot-count cycle warms the local backend before the measured set launches, and I can read the local share from the report JSON."

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The sweep harness gains a warm-start mode in which, after each slot-count restart, a short priming request is sent and must **complete locally** (`resolved_model` local, e.g. `local-qwen3/…`) — proving the first local prefill ran and `mark_warm` lifted the cold cap — before the measured request set is launched; if the priming request cannot land locally within a bounded retry budget, the run fails fast with a clear error instead of silently falling back remote.
- [ ] A configurable `--stagger-seconds N` argument (default 0 = all-at-once) spaces the *measured* request starts as requested; the fixed `INTER_REQUEST_GAP_S` constant no longer silently forces a 60 s gap, and `--stagger-seconds 0` preserves the pre-existing all-at-once launch only when explicitly intended.
- [ ] A re-run of `--sweep --resume 2 --concurrency 3 --prompt-tokens 2000` (N=2 then N=3) reports `contention.local_stream_share > 0` with **at least 2 concurrent local streams observed**, and `slot_<N>.json` records per-request `resolved_model` so the local share is auditable.
- [ ] New tests cover the warm-start gate (priming must complete locally before measured launch; bounded-retry failure path aborts the run) and the stagger math (`--stagger-seconds N` → start deltas of `N` seconds); all existing tests pass.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs-site entries — specifically the new flags in `slot_benchmark.py --help`, the sweep RESULTS_NOTE, and the reopen-conditions doc (`docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md`).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Structural root cause is proxy-side and correct behaviour:** the cold-start cap (LP-0MUCEFCAT005NFNN) exists to protect a post-restart GPU from thundering-herd prefills; it must not be weakened or disabled in `proxy/proxy/cold_start.py` for the benchmark's sake. The fix belongs in the harness (warm the backend before measuring) — or, if routed via proxy, must be opt-in and not alter the production cold-start guard.
- **Sweep lock / quiet-window constraints:** the run must still pass `scripts/slot_sweep_preflight.py` (quiet window, config unchanged, `session_slot_pool_size` restored after the sweep — AC5 of LP-0MVAZPQUM006EAC7).
- **Do not corrupt production state:** slot cache and prompt cache preserved by default (`--clean-cache` remains OFF); `proxy/config.yaml` restored in `finally`.
- **Client-timeout budget:** agentic turns target up to 18 000 output tokens (~600 s); priming must be a *small* request (e.g. "Say Hi" / minimal prompt) so it completes within the 1 200 s client timeout and the cold grace window (default 120 s).
- **No ad-hoc full-suite runs during implementation; all test invocations go through the test skill.**

## Existing state

- Harness: `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` — existing flags: `--sweep`, `--slots`, `--all`, `--test`, `--dry-run`, `--resume`, `--skip-restart`, `--warmup` (concurrent warmup task, **not** a gate), `--clean-cache`, `--phase`, `--concurrency`, `--prompt-tokens`, `--log-dir`, `--no-health-samples`. `INTER_REQUEST_GAP_S = 60.0` hard-codes a 60 s stagger inside `run_slot_benchmark`.
- Cold-start admission: `proxy/proxy/cold_start.py` — `note_model_loaded()` arms the window on restart; `mark_warm()` lifts the cap on first data chunk (called from `proxy/proxy/router.py` and `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`); cap `effective_max_concurrent` defaults to 1 while cold.
- Local share metric: `derive_local_stream_share()` in `slot_benchmark.py` computes `local_stream_share` from per-request `resolved_model` (`X-Resolved-Model` response header); `is_local_resolved_model()` classifies `local-qwen3/…` as local.
- Evidence: `proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_20261023/RESULTS_NOTE.md` (both runs INVALID, 0.0% local share, root-cause write-up) and `sweep_n2_n3.log` (request 1 stuck in `backend busy (health check timeout)` for the entire window).
- Verdict doc: `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` — re-open condition #1 is exactly this item.

## Desired change

Add to `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py`:

1. **Warm-start priming gate** (`--warm-start` flag or enabled by default in `--sweep` mode): after the restart + `Llama-server ready`, send one small priming request (short prompt, 1 turn) and poll its completion. Success = request completed with `is_local_resolved_model(resolved_model)` true (local prefill done ⇒ `mark_warm` fired). Only then create the measured request tasks. Bounded retry/timeout (e.g. re-send up to K times within the cold grace window); treat persistent failure as a run error with a diagnostic message (`cold_start.is_cold()` reference / `local_dispatch_denied` log lines), never a silent remote fallback.
2. **Configurable `--stagger-seconds N`** (default 0): replace the hard-coded `INTER_REQUEST_GAP_S * idx` delay with `stagger_seconds * idx`; keep the existing per-request concurrent-overlap semantics (requests still run concurrently once started). Default 0 preserves today's all-at-once launch for explicit use; the sweep invocation passes `--stagger-seconds 0` or a small value explicitly.
3. **Test mode compat:** `--test` ("Say Hi" connectivity check) still works and can double as the priming probe.

Design note (why the warm-start gate, not stagger alone): the 2026-10-23 log already had a 60 s stagger active, yet request 1 never completed a local prefill (`backend busy (health check timeout)`), so `mark_warm` never fired and all measured requests fell back remote. A stagger alone cannot fix a first-request-that-never-lands; only a gate that *proves* a local prefill completed before the measured set launches can. The priming request is also the only harness-visible proof of `cold_start.is_cold() == False` (the state is in-process, not exposed via `/health`).

## Key Files:

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` — add `--warm-start` gate + `--stagger-seconds`; rework `run_slot_benchmark` task creation (priming phase before measured set); replace `INTER_REQUEST_GAP_S` usage.
- `proxy/proxy/cold_start.py` — **reference only** (do not weaken the guard); may warrant a `__main__`-adjacent probe or a comment cross-ref, not production changes.
- `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` — update re-open condition #1 evidence once a valid run lands.
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_20261023/RESULTS_NOTE.md` — reference/limitations; future valid-run results go in a new results dir.
- `tests/` — new unit tests for the priming gate + stagger math (follow existing harness-test conventions, e.g. `tests/test_slot_sweep_preflight.py`).

## Related work

- `LP-0MVK09622002CRMR` — Record slot-count verdict and reconcile with projection (discovered-from source; held verdict awaiting this item).
- `LP-0MVK096GF0038FTH` — Execute N=2/N=3/N=4 slot sweep in a quiet window (produced the INVALID 0.0%-local-share results).
- `LP-0MVAZPQUM006EAC7` — Slot sweep 1/2/3 with recorded results (AC5 config-drift guard).
- `LP-0MUCEFCAT005NFNN` — Cold-start admission control (proxy mechanism being worked around).
- `LP-0MVLHNJ3W007T319` — slot_benchmark: record finish_reason per request (related harness gap; listed in reopen doc as a precondition).
- `LP-0MRWUAXRX004JZSO` — Add staggered start support to run_benchmark.py (precedent for `--stagger` flag in the sibling harness `run_benchmark.py`).
- `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md`, `proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_20261023/RESULTS_NOTE.md` — decision + evidence docs.

## Assumptions & risks

- **Assumption (design choice):** implement the **warm-start priming gate** as the primary fix (description: "any one is enough"), with `--stagger-seconds` as a complementary control. Rationale: the 60 s stagger already present was proven insufficient in the 2026-10-23 log. Recorded in the Appendix; producer may override at review (alternative: stagger-only, or single-turn production-sized requests).
- **Risk — priming request could also be denied** if llama-server is still settling (observed `backend busy (health check timeout)`): mitigate with bounded retries within the grace window and fail-fast diagnostic on persistent failure; do NOT measure 0.0%-local-share as a valid result.
- **Risk — valid-run scope creep:** a successful sweep re-run (this item's goal) may invite re-deciding slot count (LP-0MVK09622002CRMR verdict) — that is a separate review decision, out of scope here; record as follow-up, not scope.
- **Risk — warm-start hides cold-start behaviour:** the gate intentionally measures *warm* concurrency only (matches production: sessions arrive staggered and warm); cold-start behaviour stays the proxy's domain and is not what this sweep evaluates.
- **Risk — auditability:** local share is derived from `X-Resolved-Model` headers; ensure priming request and measured requests record `resolved_model` so the share is provable.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview was conducted: this item was auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker (headless, no operator present), and the seed description is exceptionally detailed (root cause, three accepted capabilities, embedded draft AC, and explicit "any one is enough" discretion). The design decision below is therefore recorded as a research-backed assumption for producer review rather than an interactive answer.

- Q (design decision — routed to producer for confirmation at review): "Which of the three accepted capabilities should this item implement — `--stagger-seconds N`, a warm-start priming gate, or single-turn production-sized requests?" — **Recommended:** warm-start priming gate + configurable `--stagger-seconds` — a fixed stagger alone is proven insufficient by the 2026-10-23 log (60 s stagger active, yet request 1 never completed a local prefill, so `mark_warm` never fired); the gate is the only harness-visible proof of `is_cold() == False`. Answer (Map): assumption recorded 2026-10-24; no interactive answer available (headless dispatch). Source: `proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_20261023/sweep_n2_n3.log` (staggered starts at 21:08:29/21:09:29/21:10:29 with request 1 stuck in `backend busy (health check timeout)`), `RESULTS_NOTE.md` ("Why local share is 0 %"), `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` (`INTER_REQUEST_GAP_S = 60.0`).
- Q (scope): "Should the proxy's cold-start cap be changed to make the sweep pass?" — Answer (research): **No.** The cap (LP-0MUCEFCAT005NFNN) protects the GPU from post-restart prefill floods in production; weakening it is out of scope and would corrupt the very behaviour the projection models. Fix belongs in the harness. Source: `proxy/proxy/cold_start.py` docstring.

Duplicate-work check performed: `wl search "slot sweep"` / `"warm-start"` / `"stagger"` — no overlapping open item found; `LP-0MRWUAXRX004JZSO` (run_benchmark.py `--stagger`) is completed and targets the sibling harness, not `slot_benchmark.py` — noted as related precedent, not a duplicate.

---

# Goal

Close out the observational acceptance criteria of **LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM** (false `saturated` capacity signal) once the new proxy code is running on `dev`.

## Background

The gate-side fix (commits 56a3a28a, 2d2b6b51) makes `/llama/local/status` truthful: stale slot detail degrades `capacity_hint` to `idle` (never `saturated`) without live work; `local_active_query` is derived from active dispatch records; an unloaded model (HTTP 400/404 from llama-server's router `/slots?model=`) is treated as fresh absence (fail open on the pool); and `local_prefills_in_flight` publishes only markers backed by a live record.

What cannot be verified inside the implementation session is the overnight behaviour.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Over a night window comparable to 2026-10-22 (20:00-07:00 local), `slots_stale` is <5% of status polls (was 79.5%), and `capacity_hint=saturated` is only observed while the proxy has live local work.
- AC2: herdr downtime dispatches on a genuinely idle GPU night reach the Oct 20/21 baseline (>=10 dispatches/night) with the same work-item queue (was 1 in ~9 h).
- AC3: Any residual stale polls are attributable (documented cause, e.g. transient /slots 500 vs idle-model unload) in the nightly usage report.
- AC4: Report the measured numbers on LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM and close this item.

## References

- Parent fix: LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM (discovered-from)
- Evidence window: `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` (2026-10-23 05:00 run), `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.*`

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy-usage analyst, I want the analysis pipeline to parse the
`routing_skip_provider_context` lines the proxy already emits, so the largest
unparsed source of session-bearing fallback evidence is no longer discarded.

## Why

The proxy logs a session-bearing skip for every provider whose context ceiling
is exceeded:

```
routing_skip_provider_context provider=munitoai-free type=remote
  status=provider_context_exceeded estimated_tokens=195787 limit=150000
  reason=provider_context_exceeded session=<uuid>
```

There are **8,828 such lines in the 24h window** (2026-10-23 10:52 ->
2026-10-24 10:52), and
`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` has no pattern for
them at all — they are silently skipped. `provider_context_exceeded` is 17.6%
(1,728 events) of the fallback-reason table, currently attributable only via
session-less `Fallback triggered` lines.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `log_parser.py` parses `routing_skip_provider_context` into a
  structured event kind (e.g. `provider_context_skip`) carrying at minimum
  `session`, `provider`, `reason`, `estimated_tokens`, `limit`, and
  `type`, plus the source file/line for evidence.
- AC2: `aggregation.py` includes the new event in per-session attribution with
  a defined precedence relative to `routing_skip_local` and `Fallback
  triggered` (documented), so a session's own provider-context skip is
  preferred over a nearest-line guess.
- AC3: `reporting.py` reports provider-context skips in a dedicated
  breakdown (count, % of skips, standard/low split, provider breakdown) and
  the per-session fallback reason reflects an own line where one exists.
- AC4: `recommendations.py` gains context-pressure advice driven by the new
  provider-context skip data — alongside the existing advice derived from
  `large_context_bypass` / `context_too_large` counts — reporting count, share
  of fallbacks, standard/low split and the `limit` value that explains which
  ceiling was hit.
- AC5: Tests: `tests/fixtures.py` gains real-shaped fixture lines;
  `test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` covers parsing, aggregation attribution and
  report rendering; `test_availability_classification.py` and any hourly
  activity assertions stay green.
- AC6: `REFERENCE.md` documents the new event kind, the attribution
  precedence, and the report section; `SKILL.md` output description is updated
  if the report gains a subsection.
- AC7: Other log consumers that should account for the line are audited and
  updated where relevant: `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py`,
  `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`, `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`.
- AC8: Historical windows remain parseable (no hard dependency on fields
  absent from older lines); absent `limit` degrades gracefully.
- AC9: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Notes

- This is analysis-side only: no proxy change required, since the line is
  already emitted with a session id.
- Related: adding session context to `Fallback triggered` (separate item)
  reduces reliance on this line, but parsing it is still needed to report
  provider-context pressure with provider/limit detail.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — new
  `routing_skip_provider_context` pattern and event kind (AC1)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — per-session
  attribution precedence: own provider-context skip line before nearest-line
  `Fallback triggered` guess (AC2)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — dedicated
  provider-context-skip breakdown section (AC3)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/recommendations.py` — context-pressure
  advice using the new event and its `limit` (AC4)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py`,
  `tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`, `tests/test_availability_classification.py`
  — fixtures and tests (AC5)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`, `SKILL.md` — documentation (AC6)
- `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py`,
  `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`, `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`
  — audited consumers (AC7)

## Related work

- **LP-0MVK1Q99B0035OOE** (Tests: cost/volume metrics and provider-context
  events; parent LP-0MVIAEARO0001O7R) — overlapping test scope: its AC1 pins a
  parser unit test asserting the six fields of `routing_skip_provider_context`
  in `tests/fixtures.py` / `test_llama_log_parser.py`. That item is a test-first
  pin for the cost/volume epic (intentionally red until its implementation
  child lands). It does **not** cover aggregation attribution, reporting,
  recommendations or docs — those remain in scope here. Reuse its fixture line
  verbatim rather than duplicating it.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-24 — Plan skill run (LP-0MVMBM1Y3001TPRT). Effort/risk pre-check:
  Extra Small / Low → planning skipped; six automated review stages applied.
  Changes: **AC4 corrected** (recommendations.py currently derives
  context-pressure advice from `large_context_bypass` / `context_too_large`
  counts, not `provider_context_exceeded`); **`## Key Files` added**;
  **`## Related work` overlap note added** re LP-0MVK1Q99B0035OOE. No child
  items created (single-slice task); stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer and as the proxy-usage analyst, I want every `Fallback
triggered` log line to identify the session and the attempt it belongs to, so
per-session fallback attribution stops relying on a "nearest line within 60
seconds" guess.

## Why

`Fallback triggered` is now the only structured decision line with no session
context. `routing_skip_local`, `routing_skip_provider_context`, `routing_hop`,
`Stream started`, `Stream finished`, `local_dispatch_denied` and even
`[local] POST` all carry a session id.

Consequence observed in the 2026-10-23/24 window: a session with no
`routing_skip_local` line of its own inherited an unrelated
`munitoai-free -> opencode-go` spill as its fallback reason. 11 of the 26
sessions that used local were labelled `rate_limited` this way, while the real
cause was `local_dispatch_denied` (lease held by another session). Example:
herdr-1792767061-1282111-17770 has no skip and no fallback line at all, only
lease denials.

The session id is already available in scope: `_budget_session_id` is resolved
in `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` (proxy/proxy/provider.py ~line 8177).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The three `Fallback triggered` emit sites (proxy/proxy/provider.py
  `_handle_streaming_success`, `_build_fallback_success_response`, and the
  third site `_resolve_reasoning_content_promotion` around line 7563) include
  `session=<uuid|unknown>` on the log line, threaded from the request's
  resolved session id.
- AC2: The same line carries an attempt/step index (e.g. `attempt=N`) so two
  fallbacks from the same session in the same second are distinguishable.
- AC3: When `reason` is budget-driven (`rate_limited*`), the line also carries
  the budget evidence already computed by
  `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py`: `limit=`, `remaining=`, `waited=` (only
  for those reasons; no behaviour change to the decision itself).
- AC4: Existing lines keep their current prefix and key=value shape where
  possible; any consumer regex tolerant of extra trailing fields continues to
  work (verify, don't assume).
- AC5: The usage-analysis skill consumes the new fields:
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` (parse `session`,
  `attempt`, budget fields on the fallback event),
  `aggregation.py` (`_attribute_fallback` uses the session's own fallback line
  before any nearest-line heuristic), `reporting.py` (per-session reason is
  sourced from own evidence; expose explicit `no remote fallback` /
  `lease/concurrency denied` / `unattributed` states instead of inheriting),
  and `recommendations.py` where reason counts are cited.
- AC6: Skill tests updated/added: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/`
  (`fixtures.py`, `test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`,
  `test_availability_classification.py`) cover session-bearing fallback

- The emit-site helpers are called from **two sibling fallback cycles** (7

  session var `_session_id`). Thread the session id into the three helpers
  from each caller — do not assume `_budget_session_id` is in scope at every
  call site.
- AC4 "verify, don't assume" answers: three consumers are **end-anchored**
  and will break unless updated — `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py`
  (`RE_FALLBACK`, `reason=([\w ]+)$`), `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py`
  (line 46, `reason=[A-Za-z0-9_ ]+)$`), `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`
  (line 81, `reason=(?P<reason>\S+)$`). New fields placed after `reason=`
  break all three; place new fields consistently and update these regexes
  (log_parser is AC5; munitoai_budget_eval and slot-persistence-correlate
  are AC7).
- `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py` does **not** parse
  `Fallback triggered` (docstring/report text only) — verified pass-through,

- `proxy/proxy/ui.py` contains no `Fallback triggered` reference — verified
  unaffected (AC7's pass-through check).

  (`limit_rpm`), `remaining=`, `waited=` (`waited_seconds`); emit only when
  `reason` starts with `rate_limited` (AC3).

  asserting log text → `log_parser`/`aggregation`/`reporting`/`recommendations`

  parse (absent field degrades to the current nearest-line heuristic), so

- Do not change the fallback *decision* logic; this is a logging/observability

data.description:
## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the proxy to record real prompt/completion token usage
for local streams, so that (a) local cache-credit and context accounting can
work from measured data and (b) the usage-analysis report can measure actual
local prompt sizes instead of showing them as unknown.

## Why (evidence)

Local `Stream finished` lines **never carry `tokens=`**:

- 225 of 225 local `Stream finished` lines in the window 2026-10-23 10:52 ->
  2026-10-24 10:52 have no token field;
- **0** lines with `tokens=` exist in the entire log archive (2026-10-17 ->
  2026-10-24) for `provider=local`.

Consequences:

1. **The usage-based cache-credit path is dead for local.** In
   `proxy/router.py` (~line 566) `update_cached_ratio()` and
   `record_prompt_prefix()` are only called when the response carries a usage
   block with `prompt_tokens > 0`. Because local never reports usage, the
   expected-reuse credit (`LP-0MVI2XOTY008Q4UV`) can never be earned from
   measured tokens. Credit today comes only from the slot-snapshot seeding
   path (655 `slot_save success` events in the archive), so a session whose
   first local dispatch did not produce a snapshot stays permanently "cold"
   (ratio 0.00) and is then bypassed by the 38K cold-cache rule on every later
   turn.
2. **The report cannot measure local context.** In the window, 3 of the 26
   sessions that used local had no context size at all, and the per-model
   token table attributes local tokens only via sessions whose *initial*
   provider was local — not via actual local streams.
3. Two current analysis outputs are therefore guesses rather than
   measurements: per-session local prompt sizes, and the cache-state
   attribution used in the skip-reason explanation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Local `Stream finished` lines include `tokens=prompt/completion/total`
  with values taken from llama-server's reported usage (its response/`usage`
  payload or `/slots` accounting — whichever is authoritative), for
  non-streaming and streaming paths.
- AC2: `update_cached_ratio()` and `record_prompt_prefix()` therefore fire for
  local streams with measured values, so the expected-reuse credit is earned
  from data rather than only from a saved slot snapshot. Verify with a test
  that a 30K local turn followed by a 40K total / 10K new turn routes local
  (the intended cold-cap semantics: the cap applies to NEW, uncached tokens).
- AC3: A regression test proves the sequential-caching case explicitly:
  turn 1 total 30K -> local; turn 2 total 40K with ~10K new -> still local
  (new tokens below the 38K cold cap). This is the behaviour the design
  intends and it currently cannot be demonstrated from the logs.
- AC4: The usage-analysis skill consumes the new data:
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` and
  `aggregation.py` attribute tokens to local streams, `reporting.py` reports
  real local prompt sizes and a "streams without usage" count, and the
  limitation text that currently explains missing local context is updated.
- AC5: Other log consumers relying on `tokens=` are audited:
  `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`, `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`.
- AC6: Tests: skill fixtures/tests in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` plus proxy-side tests for the emit
  path.
- AC7: `REFERENCE.md` documents local token reporting and the cold-cap
  semantics (cap applies to new/uncached tokens; total context is bounded
  separately by the warm cap).
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Notes

- Complements LP-0MVMBM6N400541EH (`tokens=missing` marker): that item makes
  absence explicit; this item fixes the root cause (local usage is never
  reported at all, so the marker would fire on every local stream).
- Do not change routing thresholds here — this is measurement plumbing, and it
  is a prerequisite for measuring any later routing change honestly.
data.title: Report real token usage for local streams (cold-cap/unlock + measurable context)
